items.stem: Which signal is best suited to finding which service in a request chain caused high end-to-end latency?

options.text: A distributed trace, because its spans show time spent in each service along the request path
options.rationale: Correct: traces break a request into spans per service, revealing where latency accrues.

options.text: A single counter metric with no labels
options.rationale: An unlabelled counter cannot localise latency to a service.
Unstructured logs alone do not reconstruct the cross-service timeline.
A screenshot is not a signal source for latency analysis.

items.explanation: Correct: traces break a request into spans per service, revealing where latency accrues.

items.stem: Which statements about metric cardinality in Prometheus are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Each unique combination of label values creates a separate time series
options.rationale: Correct: cardinality is the number of distinct label-value combinations, each a series.

options.text: Putting unbounded values like user IDs in labels can exhaust memory
options.rationale: Correct: high-cardinality labels such as user IDs cause series explosion and memory pressure.

options.text: Labels have no effect on the number of stored time series
options.rationale: Labels directly determine how many series exist.

options.text: Cardinality only matters for logs, not metrics
options.rationale: Cardinality is a central concern for metrics in Prometheus.

items.explanation: Correct: cardinality is the number of distinct label-value combinations, each a series.; Correct: high-cardinality labels such as user IDs cause series explosion and memory pressure.

items.stem: Why alert on an SLO burn rate rather than on raw CPU utilisation?

options.text: Burn-rate alerts track consumption of the error budget tied to user-facing reliability, reducing noise from benign resource spikes
options.rationale: Correct: SLO burn-rate alerting focuses on user impact and the error budget, not incidental resource use.

options.text: CPU utilisation cannot be measured by Prometheus
options.rationale: CPU can be measured; the point is relevance, not capability.

options.text: Burn-rate alerts remove the need for dashboards
options.rationale: Alerts and dashboards serve different purposes.

options.text: Raw CPU always correlates exactly with user experience
options.rationale: High CPU does not reliably indicate user-facing failure.

items.explanation: Correct: SLO burn-rate alerting focuses on user impact and the error budget, not incidental resource use.
